title: English Language Assessment Grade 6 (English Gr.6 - MidFinal)

sections.name: Section A: Multiple Choice (ปรนัย)
Section B: True / False (ถูก / ผิด)
Section C: Scenario-Based (สถานการณ์จำลอง)
Section D: Short Answer (อัตนัย / อธิบายความรู้)

questions.question: She ________ to school by bus every morning.
questions.explanation: The subject 'She' is singular third-person, so the verb in Present Simple Tense takes -s -> goes.

questions.question: Look! The children ________ football in the playground right now.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'right now' indicates an action in progress at the moment of speaking -> Present Continuous (are playing).

questions.question: Yesterday, Tom ________ a new bicycle at the mall.
questions.explanation: The word 'Yesterday' indicates past time in Past Simple Tense -> bought.

questions.question: They ________ to Japan next month. They have already booked the tickets.
questions.explanation: Prior arrangement/plan with booked tickets uses 'be going to' for future -> are going to visit.

questions.question: This is Mary's book. It belongs to ________.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to', we use the Object Pronoun 'her'.

questions.question: My birthday is ________ July 15th.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for specific calendar dates (July 15th).

questions.question: We usually have lunch ________ 12:30 p.m.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for specific clock times (12:30 p.m.).

questions.question: There isn't ________ milk left in the refrigerator.
questions.explanation: We use 'any' in negative sentences with uncountable nouns (milk).

questions.question: How ________ students are there in your classroom?
questions.explanation: We use 'How many' for plural countable nouns (students).

questions.question: An elephant is ________ than a tiger.
questions.explanation: Comparative degree of single-syllable adjective 'big' with CVC pattern doubles last consonant -> bigger.

questions.question: Mount Everest is the ________ mountain in the world.
questions.explanation: Superlative degree with 'the' for 'high' is highest.

questions.question: You ________ stop when the traffic light turns red.
questions.explanation: Expressing mandatory rule or legal obligation uses 'must'.

questions.question: If you have a toothache, you ________ see a dentist.
questions.explanation: Giving medical advice uses 'should' (should see a dentist).

questions.question: He was tired, ________ he continued working to finish the project.
questions.explanation: Connecting contrasting ideas (tired vs continued working) uses 'but'.

questions.question: If it ________ tomorrow, we will stay at home and watch movies.
questions.explanation: First Conditional structure: If + Present Simple (rains), Will + V.1.

questions.question: A person who puts out fires and saves people is a ________.
questions.explanation: A firefighter puts out fires and rescues people.

questions.question: A ________ flies airplanes and travels around the world.
questions.explanation: A pilot flies airplanes.

questions.question: My uncle works in a restaurant kitchen. He prepares delicious food. He is a ________.
questions.explanation: A chef cooks food in a kitchen.

questions.question: Sam ate too much ice cream. Now he has a ________.
questions.explanation: Eating too much ice cream causes a stomachache.

questions.question: When you have a high body temperature, you have a ________.
questions.explanation: High body temperature is a fever.

questions.question: Where do you go to send letters and parcels?
questions.explanation: Letters and parcels are handled at the post office.

questions.question: A place where you can borrow and read books for free is a ________.
questions.explanation: A library offers free book reading and borrowing.

questions.question: Lemons taste ________, while sugar tastes sweet.
questions.explanation: Lemons taste sour.

questions.question: Which animal is known as the 'Ship of the Desert'?
questions.explanation: The camel is known as the Ship of the Desert.

questions.question: It is ________ today. Don't forget to take an umbrella with you!
questions.explanation: Taking an umbrella indicates rainy weather.

questions.question: Go ________ ahead and turn left at the traffic lights.
questions.explanation: 'Go straight ahead' means moving forward in a line.

questions.question: A period of ten years is called a ________.
questions.explanation: A 10-year period is a decade.

questions.question: We use a ________ to measure length and draw straight lines.
questions.explanation: A ruler is used for drawing lines and measuring length.

questions.question: After dinner, I always help my mother wash the ________.
questions.explanation: Washing tableware after meals is 'wash the dishes'.

questions.question: A large vehicle that carries many passengers on fixed city routes is a ________.
questions.explanation: A bus carries many passengers along city routes.

questions.question: You see a sign 'NO SWIMMING' at the beach. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 'NO SWIMMING' means swimming is prohibited.

questions.question: A sign showing 'QUIET PLEASE' in a library asks people to ________.

options.ข: stop talking and make no noise

questions.explanation: 'QUIET PLEASE' requests silence.

questions.question: A sign with 'DON'T FEED THE ANIMALS' at the zoo warns visitors ________.

options.ข: not to give food to animals

questions.explanation: 'DON'T FEED THE ANIMALS' forbids feeding animals.

questions.question: A: Thank you very much for your help.
questions.explanation: Standard polite response to 'Thank you' is 'You're welcome'.

questions.question: A: I'm really sorry for breaking your ruler.
questions.explanation: Standard response to an apology is 'Don't worry about it'.

questions.question: A: Can I borrow your pencil, please?
questions.explanation: Handing something over upon request uses 'Sure, here you are.'

questions.question: A: What would you like to order, sir?

options.ข: I'd like a fried rice and an iced tea
options.ค: I go to school by bus

questions.explanation: Ordering food uses 'I'd like...'

questions.question: A: Excuse me, how can I get to the train station?

options.ข: Go straight for two blocks, it's on your left

questions.explanation: Giving direction response: 'Go straight for two blocks, it's on your left.'

questions.question: A: How much is this blue T-shirt?
questions.explanation: Answering price question 'How much is...' requires price amount 'It's 250 Baht'.

questions.question: A: What is the weather like today in London?
questions.explanation: Answering weather question uses weather description 'It's cold and rainy'.

questions.question: Read the passage: 'Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are great swimmers. They live in cold places like Antarctica and eat fish.' What do penguins eat?
questions.explanation: According to the text: '...and eat fish.'

questions.question: From the penguin passage, where do penguins live?
questions.explanation: According to the text: 'They live in cold places like Antarctica.'

questions.question: Read the note: 'Dear Students, The school library will be closed this Friday for maintenance. Please return all borrowed books by Thursday. Thank you.' Why is the library closed on Friday?
questions.explanation: According to the text: 'closed this Friday for maintenance'

questions.question: When must students return their borrowed books according to the note?
questions.explanation: According to the text: 'Please return all borrowed books by Thursday'

questions.question: On Halloween (October 31st), children wear costumes and go door-to-door saying '________!'.
questions.explanation: Halloween tradition phrase is 'Trick or Treat!'

questions.question: What food is traditionally eaten during Thanksgiving dinner in the USA?
questions.explanation: Traditional Thanksgiving dish is roast turkey.

questions.question: Who brings presents to children on Christmas Eve according to Western legend?
questions.explanation: Santa Claus brings presents on Christmas Eve.

questions.question: The Harry Potter books ________ by J.K. Rowling.
questions.explanation: Passive Voice in past tense: object + were written.

questions.question: She is a doctor, ________?
questions.explanation: Affirmative main statement requires negative question tag -> isn't she?

questions.question: You didn't go to school yesterday, ________?
questions.explanation: Negative main statement requires positive question tag -> did you?

questions.question: The man ________ lives next door is a famous artist.
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun referring to a person as subject is 'who'.

questions.question: This is the house ________ I was born.
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun referring to a place is 'where'.

questions.question: Peter ________ arrives late for class because he gets up very early.
questions.explanation: Getting up early implies he 'never' arrives late.

questions.question: Neither John nor his friends ________ coming to the party tonight.
questions.explanation: With 'Neither A nor B', verb agrees with the closer subject 'his friends' (plural) -> are.

questions.question: Every student in the classroom ________ a uniform.
questions.explanation: 'Every + singular noun' takes a singular verb -> wears.

questions.question: She was very ________ when she won first prize in the singing contest.
questions.explanation: Winning first prize makes a person excited.

questions.question: To protect our Earth, we should ________ plastic bags and recycle paper.
questions.explanation: Environmental conservation advocates reducing plastic bag usage.

questions.question: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today. What does 'put off' mean?
questions.explanation: Phrasal verb 'put off' means postpone or delay.

questions.question: Which month comes right after August?
questions.explanation: September immediately follows August.

questions.question: What do you say to someone who is going to take an exam?
questions.explanation: Encouragement phrase for test takers is 'Good luck!'

questions.question: In English, the Present Continuous Tense is formed using 'Subject + is/am/are + V.-ing'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Present Continuous formula is Subject + is/am/are + V.-ing.

questions.question: The plural form of the word 'child' is 'childs'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. The plural form of child is 'children'.

questions.question: The word 'water' is an uncountable noun, so we cannot say 'two waters'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Water is uncountable and requires containers like 'two glasses of water'.

questions.question: We use the preposition 'at' before days of the week, such as 'at Monday'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Days of the week take preposition 'on' (on Monday).

questions.question: The comparative form of 'good' is 'gooder'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. The irregular comparative form of good is 'better'.

questions.question: The superlative form of 'beautiful' is 'the most beautiful'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Three-syllable adjectives use 'the most beautiful' in superlative.

questions.question: A 'dentist' is a doctor who takes care of people's teeth.
questions.explanation: Correct. A dentist specializes in dental healthcare.

questions.question: An 'architect' is a person whose job is to design buildings.
questions.explanation: Correct. An architect plans and designs building structures.

questions.question: An 'aquarium' is a building where historical objects are kept and displayed.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Historical objects are displayed in a museum; aquariums display aquatic life.

questions.question: When the weather forecast says 'foggy', it means the sky is clear and very sunny.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'Foggy' means thick fog obscuring visibility, not clear and sunny.

questions.question: The possessive adjective for 'they' is 'their' when used before a noun (e.g., their house).
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Their' is the possessive adjective preceding nouns.

questions.question: The modal verb 'mustn't' means 'do not have to' (you can choose whether to do it or not).
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'Mustn't' means strict prohibition, while 'don't have to' means lack of necessity.

questions.question: The expression 'quarter past eight' means 8:15.
questions.explanation: Correct. A quarter (15 minutes) past eight equals 8:15.

questions.question: The expression 'half past ten' means 10:45.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'Half past ten' means 10:30. 10:45 is 'quarter to eleven'.

questions.question: The past simple form of the verb 'go' is 'went'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Past simple V.2 of 'go' is 'went'.

questions.question: The past simple form of the verb 'teach' is 'teached'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Irregular past simple V.2 of 'teach' is 'taught'.

questions.question: A sign 'FRAGILE' on a package means the item inside breaks easily and should be handled with care.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'FRAGILE' indicates delicate, breakable contents.

questions.question: When someone says 'Bless you!' after you sneeze, it is a polite social custom in English culture.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Bless you!' is standard social etiquette after someone sneezes.

questions.question: We use 'a loaf of' to count bread, e.g., 'a loaf of bread'.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'A loaf of' is the quantifier unit for bread.

questions.question: We use 'a bar of' to count water, e.g., 'a bar of water'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. 'A bar of' is used for soap or chocolate; water uses 'a bottle of' or 'a glass of'.

questions.question: Christmas Day is celebrated annually on December 25th.
questions.explanation: Correct. Christmas Day falls on December 25th.

questions.question: On Easter Sunday, children traditionally search for hidden painted eggs.
questions.explanation: Correct. Hunting Easter eggs is a traditional Easter activity.

questions.question: We use the article 'a' before words starting with a vowel sound, such as 'a apple'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Words starting with vowel sounds require article 'an' (an apple).

questions.question: We use 'an' before 'hour' because the letter 'h' is silent and it starts with a vowel sound.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Hour' has a silent 'h' and starts with vowel sound /aʊər/, taking article 'an'.

questions.question: We use the verb 'play' with sports ending in -ing, like 'play swimming' and 'play running'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Sports ending in -ing take verb 'go' (go swimming, go running).

questions.question: We use the verb 'do' with martial arts and individual exercises like 'do gymnastics' and 'do karate'.
questions.explanation: Correct. Martial arts and individual non-team exercises take verb 'do'.

questions.question: The question word 'Whose' is used to ask about ownership/possession.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Whose' inquires about possession (Whose pen is this?).

questions.question: The opposite of 'North' is 'West'.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. The opposite of North is South; West is opposite East.

questions.question: The word 'gloves' is typically used in plural form because they come in pairs for both hands.
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Gloves' is plural as it comes in a two-hand pair.

questions.question: A 'synonym' is a word that has the opposite meaning of another word.
questions.explanation: Incorrect. A synonym has the SAME meaning. Words with OPPOSITE meanings are antonyms.

questions.scenario: John is at a restaurant. He wants to order a cheeseburger, french fries, and a bottle of mineral water. How should he politely place his order to the waiter?
questions.question: Question: How should John politely state his order to the waiter?
questions.correctAnswer: John says: 'Hello! I would like to order a cheeseburger, french fries, and a bottle of mineral water, please.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Polite food ordering utilizes 'I would like to order...' (or 'I'd like...') ending with 'please'.

questions.scenario: A tourist is lost in the city and wants to find the nearest police station. He approaches a local citizen politely. What should the tourist say?
questions.question: Question: What polite phrase should the tourist use to ask for directions?
questions.correctAnswer: Tourist says: 'Excuse me, could you please tell me how to get to the nearest police station?'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Polite direction inquiry starts with 'Excuse me, could you please tell me how to get to...?'

questions.scenario: Sarah feels unwell. She has a high fever and a severe cough. The doctor asks her about her symptoms. How should Sarah describe her illness?
questions.question: Question: How should Sarah describe her symptoms to the doctor?
questions.correctAnswer: Sarah says: 'Doctor, I don't feel well. I have a high fever and a bad cough.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Symptom descriptions use 'I have a + (symptom)' structure.

questions.scenario: Ben is trying on a jacket at a clothing store. He likes it, but it is too small for him. He wants to ask the shop assistant for a larger size. What should Ben say?
questions.question: Question: How should Ben ask for a different size from the sales clerk?
questions.correctAnswer: Ben says: 'This jacket is a bit too small for me. Do you have a larger size, please?'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Stating the issue (too small) followed by request 'Do you have a larger size, please?'.

questions.scenario: Anna wants to invite her classmate Mark to go to the cinema to watch an animated movie this Saturday afternoon. How should Anna phrase her invitation?
questions.question: Question: How should Anna formulate her invitation to Mark?
questions.correctAnswer: Anna says: 'Hi Mark! Would you like to go to the cinema to watch an animated movie with me this Saturday afternoon?'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Polite activity invitations use 'Would you like to + V.1 ... with me?'

questions.scenario: David forgot his pencil case at home. He needs an eraser for his art class. He asks his desk mate Lisa. Write their borrowing dialogue.
questions.question: Question: Write a complete borrowing dialogue between David and Lisa.
questions.correctAnswer: David: 'Lisa, I forgot my pencil case today. May I borrow your eraser, please?' Lisa: 'Sure, David! Here you are.' David: 'Thank you so much!' Lisa: 'You're welcome!'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Polite borrowing uses 'May I borrow...?' Handing over uses 'Sure, here you are.'

questions.scenario: Tom and his family planned a beach trip tomorrow. Tom checks the weather forecast news. The reporter says it will be stormy with heavy rain. What advice should Tom give his family?
questions.question: Question: What advice should Tom give to his family based on the weather report?
questions.correctAnswer: Tom says: 'The weather forecast says it will be stormy tomorrow. We shouldn't go to the beach. We should stay home instead.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Giving advice uses modal verbs 'shouldn't go' and 'should stay home'.

questions.scenario: Ken accidentally knocked over a glass of water onto Jenny's notebook. Ken immediately apologizes and offers to help clean it up. Write their conversation.
questions.question: Question: Write the apology, offer of help, and forgiving response dialogue.
questions.correctAnswer: Ken: 'Oh, I'm so sorry, Jenny! I accidentally spilled water on your notebook. Let me help you wipe it dry.' Jenny: 'That's alright, Ken. Accidents happen. Thank you for your help.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Apologizing uses 'I'm so sorry...', offering help uses 'Let me help...', forgiving uses 'That's alright.'

questions.scenario: Peter wants to know what time the English class starts today and where it takes place. He asks his teacher Miss Green. Write their short dialogue.
questions.question: Question: Write the dialogue inquiring about class time and room location.
questions.correctAnswer: Peter: 'Excuse me, Miss Green. What time does our English class start today, and where is it?' Miss Green: 'It starts at 10:15 a.m. in Room 302.' Peter: 'Thank you, teacher.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Asking start time uses 'What time does... start?' and location uses 'Where is it?'

questions.scenario: The teacher introduces a new student named Kenji from Japan to the class. Kenji introduces himself briefly (name, age, country, hobby). What does Kenji say?
questions.question: Question: Write Kenji's self-introduction speech to his new classmates.
questions.correctAnswer: Kenji says: 'Hello everyone! My name is Kenji. I am 12 years old. I come from Japan. My hobby is playing football. Nice to meet you all!'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Standard self-introduction covers name, age, origin country, hobby, and polite greeting.

questions.scenario: Emma goes to the cinema. She wants to buy 2 adult tickets for the 5:00 p.m. show of 'Spider-Man'. How does she speak with the ticket cashier?
questions.question: Question: Write Emma's dialogue with the ticket cashier.
questions.correctAnswer: Emma says: 'Hello, I'd like two tickets for Spider-Man at 5:00 p.m., please.' Cashier: 'That will be 300 Baht, please.' Emma: 'Here is the money. Thank you!'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Ticket purchasing specifies number of tickets, movie title, showtime, and payment.

questions.scenario: Mike tells his friend May that he has a severe toothache and cannot eat food properly. What advice should May give to Mike?
questions.question: Question: What healthcare advice should May give to Mike?
questions.correctAnswer: May says: 'You shouldn't eat sweet candies, and you should go to see a dentist right away.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Healthcare advice includes negative suggestion (shouldn't eat candies) and positive recommendation (should see a dentist).

questions.scenario: Two friends just finished watching an action movie. Tim thought it was exciting, but Bob thought it was boring. Write their short opinion dialogue.
questions.question: Question: Write a short dialogue where two friends express differing movie opinions.
questions.correctAnswer: Tim: 'I thought the movie was really exciting! What did you think?' Bob: 'Well, to be honest, I found it a bit boring because the story was too long.'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Inquiring opinion uses 'What did you think?' and stating opinion uses 'I thought...' / 'I found it...'

questions.scenario: On Christmas Day, Jack's family decorates the Christmas tree, exchanges gifts, and wishes each other well. Write a short paragraph describing Jack's Christmas.
questions.question: Question: Write a short narrative paragraph describing Jack's Christmas activities.
questions.correctAnswer: Jack's Christmas: 'On Christmas Day, my family decorates the green Christmas tree with colorful lights and stars. We give gifts to each other and say Merry Christmas!'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Narrative covers tree decoration, gift exchange, and festive greetings.

questions.scenario: Paul invites Amy to play computer games at his house this afternoon, but Amy has to study for her English test tomorrow. How does Amy politely decline?
questions.question: Question: How should Amy politely decline Paul's invitation with a valid reason?
questions.correctAnswer: Amy says: 'Thank you for the invitation, Paul, but I'm afraid I can't. I have to study for my English exam tomorrow. Maybe next time!'
questions.explanation: Explanation: Polite refusal thanks the inviter, uses 'I'm afraid I can't', states the reason, and offers 'Maybe next time!'

questions.question: Explain the rules for changing singular nouns into plural nouns for: 1) cat -> cats, 2) bus -> buses, 3) baby -> babies, 4) man -> men. Provide explanations for each case.
questions.correctAnswer:
1) Regular nouns: Add -s (cat -> cats)
2) Nouns ending in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x: Add -es (bus -> buses)
3) Nouns ending in consonant + y: Change y to i and add -es (baby -> babies)
4) Irregular nouns: Change the internal vowel (man -> men)
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Complete the comparison table for the adjectives: 1) tall, 2) big, 3) expensive, 4) good. Write their Comparative and Superlative forms with explanations.
questions.correctAnswer:
1) tall -> taller -> the tallest (Short adjective: add -er / -est)
2) big -> bigger -> the biggest (CVC pattern: double final consonant)
3) expensive -> more expensive -> the most expensive (Long adjective: use more / most)
4) good -> better -> the best (Irregular adjective)
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.topic: Present Simple vs Present Continuous Tense
questions.question: Explain the difference in usage between Present Simple Tense and Present Continuous Tense with 1 example sentence for each.
questions.correctAnswer:
1. Present Simple Tense: Used for daily routines, habits, and general truths.
Example: He plays football every Sunday.
2. Present Continuous Tense: Used for actions happening right now at the moment of speaking.
Example: He is playing football right now.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.topic: Prepositions of Time Rules (in, on, at)
questions.question: Explain when to use the prepositions of time 'in', 'on', and 'at' with 1 example phrase for each.
questions.correctAnswer: 1. 'at': Used for specific clock times and parts of night (e.g., at 7:00 a.m., at night)\n2. 'on': Used for specific days and calendar dates (e.g., on Monday, on December 25th)\n3. 'in': Used for months, years, seasons, and parts of the day (e.g., in July, in 2026, in the morning)
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Analyze the sentence: 'The smart student quickly solved the difficult math problem.' Identify the Subject, Verb, Adjectives, and Adverb.
questions.correctAnswer:
Analysis:
- Subject: The smart student
- Verb: solved
- Adjectives: smart (modifies student), difficult (modifies math problem)
- Adverb: quickly (modifies verb solved)
- Object: the difficult math problem
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain the main rules for using 'some' and 'any' in sentences with 2 example sentences.
questions.correctAnswer:
Rules:
1. 'some': Used in affirmative positive sentences and polite offers/requests.
Example: There are some apples on the table. / Would you like some tea?
2. 'any': Used in negative sentences and questions.
Example: There isn't any milk in the fridge. / Do you have any questions?
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Describe the origin and key traditions of Halloween (date, costumes, activities, symbols) in 3-4 sentences in English.
questions.correctAnswer: Halloween is celebrated annually on October 31st in Western countries. Children dress up in fancy costumes such as ghosts, witches, or superheroes. They go door-to-door saying 'Trick or Treat!' to collect candies. People also carve pumpkins into jack-o'-lanterns with candle lights inside.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Explain the difference between 'should' and 'must' when giving instructions or advice, with 1 example for each.
questions.correctAnswer:
1. 'should': Used for giving suggestions or mild advice (what is good to do).
Example: You should drink more water when you have a cold.
2. 'must': Used for strong obligation, necessity, or strict laws/rules.
Example: You must wear a helmet when riding a motorbike.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Write a short dialogue (4 lines) between a Customer and a Waiter ordering lunch at a restaurant in English.
questions.correctAnswer:
Waiter: Good afternoon! Are you ready to order?
Customer: Yes, please. I'd like a chicken salad and a cup of green tea.
Waiter: Would you like any dessert?
Customer: No, thank you. That will be all for now.
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.

questions.question: Write a short friendly email (4-5 lines) inviting your friend to your birthday party this weekend in English.
questions.correctAnswer:
Hi Sam,
How are you? I am writing to invite you to my 12th birthday party this Saturday at 4:00 p.m. at my home. We will play games, eat delicious birthday cake, and listen to music. I hope you can come!
Best wishes,
Tom
questions.explanation: Evaluation based on grammatical correctness, clarity, and completeness of explanation.
